tool_input.command:
cd .tmp
# f2..f5 are cols 3-6; srv_f2..srv_f5 are cols 9-12
cut -d, -f3-6 joined.csv > a.txt
cut -d, -f9-12 joined.csv > b.txt
echo "=== f2-f5 train vs serve: differing lines (excl header) ==="
diff a.txt b.txt | grep -c '^<' || echo 0
echo "=== f1 vs srv_f1: side-by-side sample ==="
paste -d' ' <(cut -d, -f2 joined.csv) <(cut -d, -f8 joined.csv) | head -8
echo "=== count rows where f1 col2 == srv_f1 col8 ==="
paste -d'|' <(cut -d, -f2 joined.csv) <(cut -d, -f8 joined.csv) | awk -F'|' 'NR>1 && $1==$2{c++} END{print "identical f1:", c+0}'
tool_input.description: Compare f2-f5 columns and inspect f1

tool_input.command:
mkdir -p submission
cat > submission/answers.json <<'JSON'
{
  "feature": "f1",
  "cause": "Training/serving skew on f1. For all 200 entities present in both paths, features f2-f5 match exactly while f1 differs on every row. The relationship is srv_f1 = exp(train_f1) - 1 (i.e. train_f1 = log1p(srv_f1)). The training pipeline applies a log1p (log(1+x)) transform to f1, but the online serving path serves the raw, un-logged value, so the model receives differently-scaled f1 at inference time."
}
JSON
cat submission/answers.json
